title: Delegated Approvals and Supplier Onboarding Patterns
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:
This guide consolidates company‑wide patterns for delegated approvals, supplier onboarding, procurement thresholds, change control, data handling expectations, travel expense controls, and a small bundle of ready‑to‑use templates. It is intended for requestors, approvers, finance, security, and the people teams running supplier relationships.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference legal entities and headcount worldwide.
- Covers: access & permissions requests, change approvals touching production systems, procurement and expense approvals, supplier onboarding and offboarding, and business travel reimbursements.
- Excludes: personal reimbursements under the petty cash policy (see People Ops docs).

Principles:
- Least privilege: grants must be narrowly scoped and time‑bounded by default.
- Separation of duties: requesting, approving, and provisioning should not be the same person for privileged actions.
- Risk proportionality: higher risk or higher spend requires broader review and longer retention of evidence.
- Single source of truth: use the central request system for all approvals and maintain an auditable trail.

Access & Permissions:
1) Standard request flows:
   - Non‑privileged access (read, dev environments): request via the Access Portal; approver: team lead; auto‑granting SLA: 3 business days.
   - Privileged access (prod write, infra admin): raise an Access Request with justification, expiration window, and a scoped list of resources. Approver chain: team lead -> security reviewer -> infra owner; SLA: 5 business days.
   - Emergency access (break glass): submit an incident ticket AND a temporary access request. Temporary access duration: max 12 hours. Post‑event review required within 5 business days.

2) Delegation patterns:
   - Role owners can delegate approval rights for non‑privileged access to a named delegate for up to 6 months. Delegations must be recorded in the Access Portal and reviewed quarterly.
   - Only people with explicit delegation may approve requests under the $5k procurement equivalence threshold (see procurement table).

3) Required artifacts with every request:
   - Purpose statement (one sentence), scope (specific resources), estimated duration, business owner, and link to any relevant change ticket.

Change Management (production changes):
- Classification:
  1. Standard: low‑risk configuration or non‑customer impacting deploys. Requires code review and automated tests.
  2. Major: schema migrations, model swaps, infra changes affecting latency/costs. Requires change advisory board (CAB) approval and test plan.
  3. Emergency: restoring service or mitigating active incident. Retro review mandatory.

- Change process steps (numbered):
  1. Create change ticket in the Change System with classification, rollback plan, and verification criteria.
  2. Obtain approvals per the approval matrix (see appendix).
  3. Schedule deployment in the release calendar and notify SRE/Oncall 48 hours in advance for Major changes.
  4. Execute during approved window; collect verification evidence (logs, metrics, screenshots).
  5. Post‑change review: update the ticket with outcomes and lessons learned.

- Emergency changes:
  - Must be annotated as Emergency in the ticket and include a migration to a Standard or Major change record within 72 hours.

Data Management & Classification:
- Classification levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted.
- Minimum controls per class:
  - Public: no controls required for sharing.
  - Internal: default for most internal docs; stored in company drive with access controls.
  - Confidential: PII, contractual terms, internal roadmaps. Must be stored in enterprise document store with link‑level ACL and retention of 3 years.
  - Restricted: customer data, secrets, audit logs — encryption at rest and in transit, strict RBAC, and monitoring; retention and deletion policies applied per contract.

- Data handling checklist for projects:
  - Identify classification at project initiation.
  - Map data flows and storage locations.
  - Document retention and deletion schedule.
  - Review with Security for Restricted/Confidential categories.

Procurement & Expenses:
- Approval thresholds (summary):
| Item type | Threshold (USD) | Approver | Additional requirement |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Low cost tools / SaaS seats | <= 2,000 | Team lead | Finance notification |
| Operational subscriptions / infra | 2,001 – 25,000 | Dept manager + Finance | Security review if infra impact |
| Strategic contracts / one‑time purchases | 25,001 – 150,000 | VP + Procurement | Legal review and 3 bids recommended |
| Strategic >150,000 | >150,000 | CFO + Head of Procurement | Legal/Audit & Exec sponsor |

- Expense policy highlights:
  - Travel: employees must use preferred travel partners; early booking encouraged. Domestic airfare under $1,200 without approval for the mid‑tier class. Exceptions need manager justification.
  - Meals: capped per diem limits by city band; receipts required for amounts > $75.
  - Personal spending: must not be charged to company accounts.

- Procurement process (steps):
  1. Create a Purchase Request with estimated total and business justification.
  2. Request quotes (minimum 1 for <$25k, minimum 3 for >=$25k unless sole source).
  3. Submit to approver per thresholds. 
  4. Procurement creates PO, negotiates T&Cs, and routes to Legal if required.
  5. Supplier setup (see onboarding below) before payment.

Vendor Onboarding & Lifecycle:
- Pre‑qualification checklist:
  - Corporate registration, tax form, W‑9 (US) or local equivalent, conflict of interest statement.
  - Security questionnaire for vendors touching data or infra (SIG Lite or comparable).
  - Insurance proof for vendors with field operations.

- Onboarding steps (sequence):
  1. Intake: Requestor files Vendor Intake form with scope and expected spend.
  2. Procurement performs supplier due diligence (KYC, risk rating).
  3. Security review if vendor will access company systems or data.
  4. Legal prepares contract with standard Redwood clauses and any negotiated modifications.
  5. Finance sets payment terms and creates supplier profile.
  6. Operational kickoff and technical onboarding.

- Lifecycle governance:
  - Annual review for any supplier with >$50k annual spend or access to Restricted data.
  - Offboarding: ensure account terminations, return of assets, and revocation of secrets within 5 business days from contract end.

Travel Policy (key controls):
- Booking and class of service: employees are expected to select economy or company‑preferred fare. Manager approval required for premium or change in class.
- Expense documentation: receipts required for all expenses above $25; foreign currency receipts should be translated.
- Duty of care: travel registry for all overnight trips; People Ops maintains emergency contact procedures.

Templates & Forms (where to find them):
- Vendor Intake Form: link to central template in the templates repository.
- Access Request Template: prefilled fields for purpose, scope, owner, and duration.
- Change Request Template: fields for risk classification, rollback plan, test plan, and verification metrics.
- Travel Expense Template: per diem calculator and currency converter.

Ownership & SLAs:
- Policy owner: Finance‑Legal (primary), Security (co‑owner for data and access controls), People Ops (travel & expense).
- SLAs:
  - Access requests: Non‑privileged 3 business days; Privileged 5 business days; Emergency immediate with 12‑hour limit.
  - Procurement approvals: up to 10 business days for >$25k (includes legal review).
  - Vendor onboarding: standard 15 business days, expedited option 5 business days with Exec sponsor.

Appendix: Example Approval Matrix
| Action | Requestor | Approver | Secondary Approver | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Add infra write role (prod) | Engineer | Team lead | Security + Infra owner | Time‑bound by default |
| New SaaS contract ($30k) | Product manager | Dept manager | Procurement + Legal | 3 bids recommended |
| Emergency DB fix | Oncall | SRE lead | Incident Commander (post‑review) | Retro within 5 days |

Quick CLI sample (example change request payload):
```json
{
  "title": "Swap model instance to quantized variant",
  "classification": "Major",
  "rollback_plan": "Rollback to previous container image v2.3.1",
  "verification": "Latency p50 < 120ms; end‑to‑end test suite pass",
  "business_owner": "alex.patel@redwood.com"
}
```

Contacts & Escalation:
- Finance Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Vendor intake and KYC: vendorops@redwood.com
- Security review requests: secureops@redwood.com
- Access Portal support: idops@redwood.com

Change Log:
- 2025‑02‑10: Created by Maya Chen (initial pattern consolidation).
- 2025‑09‑03: Added emergency access cadence and post‑change evidence requirements (reviewer: Rafael Ortiz).
- 2026‑01‑18: Added vendor annual review thresholds and expedited onboarding path (reviewer: Priya Nair).

Revision notes: This guide is a patterns document, not a substitute for specialized legal or regulatory requirements for specific engagements. Always route contract terms to Legal and raise security exceptions through the standard exception process.
